tasks.short: Agree project requirements and objectives with stakeholders.

steps.what: Read the project brief, previous decisions and stakeholder requests.

loop.input: Project brief, decision log and stakeholder requests.
loop.output: Source-linked objectives, constraints, conflicts and open questions.
loop.check: Require a source reference for each claim; flag conflicting statements for review.
loop.stop: One extraction and one repair pass per document batch; unresolved items enter the discussion brief.
loop.why_not_simpler: Objectives and constraints arrive in varied prose; fixed fields cannot capture existing documents reliably.

steps.what: Arrange stakeholder sessions and circulate the discussion brief.
Discuss needs, uncover disagreements and negotiate project priorities.
Write requirements, acceptance criteria and unresolved questions.

loop.input: Workshop notes, proposed priorities and project brief.
loop.output: Requirements draft with acceptance criteria and explicit unresolved questions.
loop.check: Link requirements to notes; separate agreed statements from proposals; review acceptance criteria.
loop.stop: One draft and one revision; missing agreement stays unresolved rather than being inferred.
loop.why_not_simpler: Turning informal discussion into testable requirements needs interpretation and writing.

steps.what: Approve the scope and objectives, or return disputed requirements.

tasks.design: A configured flow in the {CALENDAR} arranges sessions, while a bounded loop turns approved material in the {DOCS} into a discussion brief and requirements draft. The {PROJECT} links each requirement to its source and records sponsor approval before establishing the baseline.
tasks.previous_blocker: The difficult part was reaching agreement. Preparation and documentation also required reading inconsistent briefs and informal notes.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing scheduling and approval features handle coordination. Bounded extraction and drafting can reduce document work, and AI-assisted coding can shorten the build of missing links.
tasks.still_hard: Stakeholders may conceal constraints or disagree about success. Sources can be incomplete, and formal agreement still takes time.
tasks.human_edge: Recognise unspoken concerns, negotiate competing goals and distinguish polite assent from commitment.

ambition.what: Monthly scope trade-off review using unresolved requirements and delivery evidence.

tasks.altitude: The project manager spends less time preparing and rewriting workshops and more time resolving scope conflicts. They can propose scope trade-offs more often; sponsor approval rights stay unchanged.

reach.task: Define measurable benefits for proposed requirements.
reach.learn: Benefit measures, process baselines and how to test whether a requirement changes outcomes.

evidence.claim: Scheduling, version control and approval routing can use existing system configuration.
Source-linked extraction and drafting can reduce preparation while leaving agreement to people.

assumptions: Time shares are indicative priors for a mid-size European company, not measured savings.
The conversation-heavy prior fits this decomposition; preparation remains separately changeable.
Build ranges estimate one pilot with existing identity controls and accessible files or interfaces.
Routine invitations use a confirmed participant list and a discussion brief cleared for those recipients.
GDPR applies to personal data. National rules determine consultation requirements if recording or monitoring is introduced.
unknowns: Who can approve the requirements baseline?
Which sources contain client-confidential or employee personal data?
Are meeting notes available without introducing recording?
Which existing scheduling and approval features are enabled?
Which national rules and employee consultation arrangements apply?
research_questions: How reliably can extraction preserve disagreements and distinguish proposals from approved requirements?
Which requirement templates work across different project types without extensive customisation?
new_work: Review extracted constraints and drafted acceptance criteria.
Resolve missing sources and ambiguous agreement.
Maintain recipient permissions, templates and source links.
Check that amended requirements follow the approval route.

tasks.short: Estimate project staffing, resource and funding needs from objectives and schedules.

steps.what: Review objectives and schedules to identify required work and capabilities.

loop.output: Source-linked work requirements, capability needs and missing assumptions.
loop.check: Match each requirement to approved scope; require review for inferred effort or capabilities.
loop.stop: One extraction and one repair pass; uncertain requirements remain flagged for the planning discussion.
loop.why_not_simpler: Project objectives often describe outcomes in prose rather than explicit resource categories.

steps.what: Check team availability, existing assignments and approved resource capacity.
Check approved funding, committed costs and applicable cost rates.
Calculate effort, resource gaps and costs for alternative delivery plans.
Discuss feasibility and choose assumptions for the proposed resource plan.
Record and submit the staffing, resource and funding request.

tasks.design: A deterministic job on the {DATA_PLATFORM} joins authorised capacity from the {PROJECT} and {HCM} with funding and rates from the {ERP}, then calculates resource scenarios. A bounded loop extracts needs from approved documents in the {DOCS}; the project manager reviews assumptions and releases a resource request through the {WORKFLOW}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Capacity and funding used different identifiers and update cycles. Effort assumptions were held in local workbooks or people's heads.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing exports and interfaces can support repeatable joins and calculations. Bounded document extraction and faster custom coding make a small planning service more feasible.
tasks.still_hard: Availability may omit informal commitments. Effort estimates, specialist scarcity and competing projects still require negotiation.
tasks.human_edge: Judge whether a team can deliver together and recognise when apparently available capacity is unusable.

ambition.what: Weekly resource-gap review comparing scope reduction, sequencing and additional capacity.

tasks.altitude: The project manager spends less time assembling numbers and more time testing delivery options with technical leads. They gain faster recommendation cycles; staffing allocation and spending authority require separate approval.

reach.task: Check competing work against shared capacity constraints.
reach.learn: Capacity calendars, bottleneck analysis and the difference between available hours and usable capacity.

evidence.claim: Capacity joins, rate calculations and scenario comparisons are suitable for deterministic code.
Extracting capability needs from project prose can use a bounded loop with human review.
AI used for worker evaluation or certain task-allocation purposes may fall within Annex III employment provisions.

assumptions: Time shares and build ranges are planning estimates, not documented project-management results.
The gathering and calculation steps show greater deterministic potential than the judgement-heavy prior alone suggests.
Calculations use explicit effort assumptions and approved rates; the model does not invent estimates.
Capacity data excludes absence reasons and other unnecessary personal details.
The design does not rank workers or infer performance. Any such extension requires separate GDPR and EU AI Act assessment.
Access estimates include employee consultation where national rules require it; formal processes may exceed the range.
Resource requests do not themselves authorise hiring, spending or employee reassignment.
unknowns: Are resource calendars complete and current?
Can project identifiers be matched across the {PROJECT} and {ERP}?
Which cost rates and effort assumptions are approved?
Who approves resource allocation and additional funding?
Which employee data may the project manager access?
Which national consultation requirements apply?
research_questions: Which deterministic capacity rules remain useful across project types?
How should uncertainty ranges be calibrated against completed projects?
Which proposed staffing features would trigger employment-related EU AI Act obligations?
new_work: Correct unmatched project and resource identifiers.
Maintain cost rates, capacity rules and effort assumptions.
Review missing commitments and implausible scenarios.
Monitor data freshness and reconcile scenario estimates with completed work.

tasks.short: Check, present and submit project deliverables to clients.

steps.what: Collect the delivery version, acceptance criteria and quality evidence.
Check required files, version identifiers and recorded quality results.
Judge fitness for delivery and approve quality exceptions.
Assemble the client package and submission cover note.
Present the deliverable and explain limitations and acceptance arrangements.
Verify recipients and release the approved package to the client.
Record submission evidence and the next acceptance milestone.

tasks.design: The {PROJECT} and {DOCS} assemble a versioned delivery candidate, run explicit completeness checks and generate the submission package from a template. Technical sign-off enables release, the project manager approves the recipient and package in the {WORKFLOW}, and the {EMAIL} submission creates a receipt in the {PROJECT}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Delivery files, quality evidence and client requirements were stored separately. Manual assembly and mailbox records obscured which version had been approved and sent.
tasks.enabler_now: Version controls, templates and approval flows already cover much of the work. Small deterministic checks can connect these features without needing a model.
tasks.still_hard: Quality criteria vary by deliverable. A complete package can still be unsuitable, and disputed client acceptance requires human handling.
tasks.human_edge: Explain limitations honestly, judge whether exceptions are acceptable and preserve trust when a client is dissatisfied.

ambition.what: Client handover clinic for users who must operate the delivered service.

tasks.altitude: The project manager spends less time finding files and reconstructing submission history, leaving time for practical client handover. They can propose the handover clinic; technical release and contractual acceptance rights remain with their existing owners.

reach.task: Define evidence required for a project delivery release.
reach.learn: Traceability, exception severity and the distinction between checklist completeness and fitness for use.

evidence.claim: Versioned files, template assembly and approval-dependent submission support deterministic automation.
Completeness checks can reduce paperwork but cannot establish fitness for use for every deliverable.

assumptions: Time shares and build ranges estimate a pilot for one deliverable family.
The prior's coordination-heavy pattern fits, but package assembly and submission records offer substantial deterministic savings.
Required quality tests already exist; the build checks their evidence rather than creating every domain test.
The cover note uses structured fields and approved wording, so no model loop is needed.
Client feedback does not establish formal acceptance unless the contract says it does.
GDPR governs personal data in delivery packages; access and retention follow contractual requirements and applicable national rules.
unknowns: Which deliverables and quality evidence are mandatory?
Who may approve quality exceptions and client release?
What constitutes contractual submission and acceptance?
Which recipients may access each delivery package?
Can the {DOCS} preserve the released version and access evidence?
Does the process change require employee consultation under national rules?
research_questions: Which formal delivery checks can be reused across service and technical projects?
Which submission channels provide sufficient evidence under common contract terms?
new_work: Maintain delivery checklists and submission templates.
Investigate missing evidence and failed version checks.
Handle failed transmissions, client objections and acceptance exceptions.

tasks.short: Discuss project problems with the team and coordinate their resolution.

steps.what: Collect problem reports and clarify the reported impact.

loop.input: Selected problem reports and relevant project context.
loop.output: Issue summary with symptoms, reported impact, source links and missing facts.
loop.check: Preserve reported facts; mark conflicting accounts; do not infer a root cause or assign blame.
loop.stop: One extraction and one repair pass; missing facts go to the project manager.
loop.why_not_simpler: Reports use informal language and mix symptoms, opinions and incomplete facts.

steps.what: Check affected tasks, dependencies, owners and delivery dates.
Discuss causes and possible remedies with project personnel.
Choose a remedy within delegated authority or escalate the decision.
Record the agreed actions, owners, deadlines and closure criteria.

loop.input: Approved resolution decision and discussion notes.
loop.output: Proposed actions with owners, deadlines and closure criteria.
loop.check: Link every action to the decision; validate owner identifiers; require review of missing dates.
loop.stop: One extraction and one repair pass; incomplete actions stay drafts.
loop.why_not_simpler: Agreed actions are often embedded in discussion notes rather than entered as structured records.

steps.what: Chase owners by message for updates already expected in task records.
Check resolution evidence and confirm whether the issue can close.

tasks.design: A bounded loop prepares source-linked issue summaries, and the {PROJECT} shows affected dependencies before the team discusses remedies. After human approval, a second bounded extraction writes agreed actions into the {PROJECT}; configured exception notifications replace routine chasing, while technical closure stays with the technical lead.
tasks.previous_blocker: Symptoms and agreements were scattered across messages and meetings. Issue records were often updated after the discussion, creating duplicate status requests.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing task views and notifications cover dependency checks and follow-up. Bounded extraction can turn selected reports and agreed notes into reviewed records.
tasks.still_hard: Root causes can be disputed or technically uncertain. People may avoid reporting bad news, and owners still need to keep task records current.
tasks.human_edge: Create a candid discussion, separate technical disagreement from interpersonal conflict and secure credible commitments.

ambition.what: Cross-project recurring-problem clinic for shared operational blockers.

tasks.altitude: The project manager spends less time reconstructing issues and requesting duplicate updates, leaving more time for resolution discussions and recurring problems. They can convene the clinic and recommend preventive changes; technical and budget authority do not expand automatically.

reach.task: Turn recurring project blockers into recovery options.
reach.learn: Failure scenarios, recovery dependencies and when a local workaround creates wider operational risk.

evidence.claim: Dependency views and exception notifications can use existing work-management configuration.
Bounded extraction can support issue preparation and action records without automating diagnosis or negotiation.

assumptions: Time shares and build ranges are indicative pilot estimates.
The conversation-heavy prior fits; records and routine follow-up still offer separate gains.
Routine chasing disappears only when task records provide timely updates; missing updates become exceptions.
Only selected project reports are processed, rather than unrestricted mailbox or chat monitoring.
Technical leads approve remedies within delegated authority; scope, spending and staffing changes follow their separate approval routes.
GDPR applies to project communications. National rules may require consultation for changed employee-data processing; worker evaluation would need separate EU AI Act assessment.
unknowns: Where are problem reports and resolution evidence currently stored?
Do task owners update status reliably?
Which remedies can technical leads authorise?
Which message sources may be processed and retained?
Who decides closure for nontechnical issues?
Which national consultation requirements apply?
research_questions: How reliably can extraction distinguish symptoms, hypotheses and agreed actions?
Which notification rules reduce duplicate chasing without hiding stalled issues?
How can recurring problems be grouped without attributing unsupported blame?
new_work: Review extracted facts and proposed action records.
Handle missing updates and failed notification delivery.
Maintain issue categories, escalation rules and access permissions.
Check recurring-problem groupings against source evidence.

role.altitude: The week shifts from assembling briefs, reconciling planning data and chasing records toward scope trade-offs, resource discussions and client handover. The project manager gains faster access to options and evidence; formal spending, staffing, quality and acceptance rights remain separately assigned.
reach: Management analysts: connect requirements to measurable benefits.
Production planning clerks: compare shared capacity and bottlenecks.
Quality control systems managers: define release evidence and exception thresholds.
Business continuity planners: develop recovery options for recurring blockers.
skills_to_grow: Write testable requirements and explicit planning assumptions.
Interpret capacity and cost scenarios without treating estimates as facts.
Facilitate disagreement and negotiate credible commitments.
Design approval routes, exception rules and evidence checks.
Review source-linked model drafts and maintain proportionate data access.
role.ambitious_version: Provide a lightweight project decision service: regular scope and resource reviews, practical client handover clinics and cross-project problem clinics. Start with reusable templates and authorised file imports, then add integrations where access and demonstrated value justify them.
